briefings.title: Event Replay: Circle Q2 2026 Earnings Call
briefings.tldr: Circle reported a strong Q2 2026, driven by 19% year-over-year growth in USDC circulation to $73.3 billion, a record 70% share of stablecoin transaction volume in June, and the advancement of major infrastructure milestones including the launch of the Circle National Trust Bank and the upcoming ARC mainnet.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Circle reported a strong Q2 2026, driven by 19% year-over-year growth in USDC circulation to $73.3 billion, a record 70% share of stablecoin transaction volume in June, and the advancement of major infrastructure milestones including the launch of the Circle National Trust Bank and the upcoming ARC mainnet.

## Financial Results & Business Performance
- **Circulation & Minting Metrics:** 
  - **USDC Circulation:** Ended Q2 2026 at $73.3 billion, up 19% year-over-year, while average circulation hit an all-time high of $76.5 billion.
  - **Minting & Redemption:** Daily minting and redemption averaged $1.9 billion in Q2 (up 105% year-over-year), with total quarterly mint/redeem volume reaching $170 billion.
  - **Platform Holdings:** USDC held within Circle's platform infrastructure grew 106% year-over-year to $12.4 billion (17% of total circulation). Coinbase held 30% and Hyperliquid accounted for approximately 6% of circulation at quarter end.
- **Revenue & Profitability:**
  - **Total Revenue & Reserve Income:** Reached $71 million, up 7% year-over-year, supported by circulation growth and other revenue, though partially offset by a lower reserve return rate of 3.48% (down 66 bps year-on-year due to SOFR declines).
  - **Other Revenue:** Reached $34 million (up 1.4x year-over-year), driven by blockchain partnerships, though down $8 million sequentially due to moderating blockchain revenue and prioritization of ARC.
  - **Margins:** Revenue less distribution cost margin was 41.2% (up 3 percentage points year-over-year). Adjusted EBITDAR grew 8% year-over-year to $143 million with a 50% margin.
- **Other Digital Asset Growth:**
  - **EURC:** Grew 2.2x year-over-year, maintaining its position as the largest digital euro.
  - **USYC:** Grew 10x year-over-year to over $3 billion in assets, remaining the world's largest tokenized money market fund.

## Network Expansion & Strategic Partnerships
- **Coinbase Partnership Renewal:** The strategic agreement with Coinbase has been renewed on its existing terms, ensuring USDC remains central across all Coinbase products.
- **Regulatory Milestones:** Circle received its OCC National Trust Bank Charter and an additional limited purpose trust charter from the state of New York, establishing the Circle National Trust as an infrastructure bank for the internet financial system.
- **ARC Network Launch & Partnerships:**
  - **Mainet Launch:** Set to launch on September 16, 2026; testnet has processed over half a billion transactions across ~3 million wallets with near-perfect uptime, backed by a private mainet of over 100 active partners.
  - **DTCC Collaboration:** Partnering to bring tokenized securities to ARC, starting with DTC-custodied assets and expanding to repo, collateral mobility, securities lending, and corporate actions.
  - **BlackRock Integration:** BlackRock plans to deploy BUIDL on ARC with native USDC integration to enable institutional fund management within a single onchain environment.
- **Circle Payments Network (CPN):**
  - **Volume Growth:** Reached nearly $15 billion in annualized total payment volume (TPV) on a trailing 30-day basis at the end of Q2; further accelerated to **$23 billion** as of July 31st (130% growth since the last earnings report).
  - **Adoption:** Financial institution enrollment grew nearly 30% quarter-over-quarter to 175 institutions, expanding CPN's reach to more than 58 countries.

## Market Trends & Trading Infrastructure
- **Derivatives & Real-World Assets (RWAs):** On major venues like Binance and Hyperliquid, USDC's share of open interest collateral reached 40%. Notably, tokenized real-world assets reached nearly 75% of Hyperliquid's traded volume as of late Q2.
- **Prediction Markets:** Spot volume on Polymarket (a USDC distribution partner) grew over 8x year-over-year, with open interest growing more than 4x year-over-year.

## Agentic Finance & Corporate AI Transformation
- **Ecosystem Traction:** The USDC network and payment protocols like X42 handle 99.3% of agentic payments, with over 900 paid services available in Circle's agent marketplace. Cloudflare recently added agentic wallets with X42 and USDC support.
- **Internal AI Operations:** 86% of Circle employees are weekly active users of AI tools; employees shipped over 1,100 AI apps in 2026 (mostly non-technical builders), driving software development velocity up several hundred percent.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Through-Cycle Growth Framework:** Circle believes a **40% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over several years through cycle** is achievable, aligning with third-party projections for the 2030 stablecoin market ($1 trillion to $4 trillion, or 27% to 77% CAGRs) — Jeremy Fox-Geen
- **Other Revenue Guidance:** Raised the full-year other revenue guidance range to **$310 million to $330 million** (up from $150–$170 million), driven by ARC pre-sale revenues — Jeremy Fox-Geen
- **ARC Milestone Recognition:** Circle expects to achieve approximately **75% of ARC product milestones and recognize associated revenue in 2026**, including **$180 million** from the $242 million ARC token pre-sale held in Q2 — Jeremy Fox-Geen
- **RLDC Margin Outlook:** Raised the full-year revenue less distribution cost (RLDC) margin outlook range to **41.7% to 43.7%** (up from 38% to 40%), reflecting ARC revenue contributions — Jeremy Fox-Geen
- **Adjusted Operating Expenses:** Reaffirmed the full-year guidance range of **$570 million to $585 million**, while noting expectations to land at the higher end of the range due to continued platform investments — Jeremy Fox-Geen
- **CPN Monetization:** Monetization of the Circle Payments Network (CPN) will begin in the **second half of 2026** — Jeremy Allaire

## Notable Quotes
> "Circle is in a position of significant leadership. We have built deep and durable competitive modes around trust, liquidity, regulatory standing, technology, and network scale. Our position has never been stronger." — Jeremy Allaire

> "Fundamentally we are a massive future market growth stock versus a stock that returns capital to shareholders today." — Jeremy Fox-Geen

> "We view the the USDC product and the reserve income stream still is very early stage. The addressable market for money is about $120 trillion of which about half $60 trillion is non-interest earning money... we just think we're just getting going." — Jeremy Fox-Geen

briefings.title: Palantir & Ondas | Building the Future of Mission Autonomy | Episode 2
briefings.tldr: Through the newly formed Ondas Sentinel, Ondas and Palantir are unifying autonomous defense technologies—ranging from ground robotics and counter-UAS to stratospheric balloons—powered by the Skyweaver Agentic AI orchestration platform to compress military decision timelines from hours to single-digit minutes.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Through the newly formed Ondas Sentinel, Ondas and Palantir are unifying autonomous defense technologies—ranging from ground robotics and counter-UAS to stratospheric balloons—powered by the Skyweaver Agentic AI orchestration platform to compress military decision timelines from hours to single-digit minutes.

## The Changing Character of Warfare & The Shift to Scalable Mass
- **Evolution of Force Projection:** **Ryan Hartman** noted that unmanned systems combined with autonomy represent a new era of warfare, allowing forces to project power with vastly more assets and fewer personnel, matching deployments like the nearly 100% unmanned force structure currently in Southcom.
- **The Economic Problem of Exquisite Defense:** **Matt McCue** explained that traditional defense contractors rely on exquisite, high-cost technologies that fail to scale, citing the unsustainable cost of using $35,000 Patriot missiles against low-cost targets.
- **High-Rate Automotive and Autonomy Integration:** To achieve mass, **Matt McCue** highlighted how DZYNE utilized manufacturing techniques from the automotive industry and embedded full autonomy into interceptors to remove human operators from direct control loops.
- **IonStrike Rapid Development:** **Matt McCue** and **Ryan Hartman** cited *IonStrike*—a Group 3 air defense protection system built to counter Shahid-class one-way attack drones—as a core technology conceptualized and brought to a demonstrable product in just **six months** in collaboration with the U.S. Army and Air Force.

## Ondas Sentinel: From Aircraft to Architecture
- **Unified Operating Platform:** **Ryan Hartman** described Ondas Sentinel as the go-to-market business unit uniting Ondas's portfolio, built around the mission thesis of seeing further, deciding faster, and acting with purpose.
- **Multi-Domain Spectrum Coverage:** **Ryan Hartman** detailed the integrated footprint spanning from ground-layer counter-UAS and tier-1/tier-2 UAVs, through Group 4 and Group 5 UAVs (via DZYNE), up to stratospheric balloons (via World View Enterprises operating at **60,000+ feet**), noting there is virtually zero technology overlap across the acquired companies.
- **Comprehensive Counter-UAS Layer:** **Ryan Hartman** outlined a full counter-UAS continuum spanning detect, cyber-over-RF, soft kill, and kinetic kill via an expanded product family including *Iron Drone*, *Centrics*, *Drone Buster*, *Sawtooth*, and *IonStrike*.
- **Ultra Long-Endurance Persistence:** **Matt McCue** highlighted *Ultra*, an air-breathing ISR platform with **tens of thousands of flight hours** and multi-day endurance, which reduces expensive SATCOM data usage and bandwidth requirements by executing autonomy and edge effects directly at the platform level.
- **Corporate Integration via AI Agents:** **Ryan Hartman** addressed operational integration challenges, explaining that Ondas is utilizing Palantir's *Foundry* and *Warp Speed* to deploy AI agents over systems of record (ERP, inventory, financial, and manufacturing systems) to streamline post-acquisition integration without halting business operations.

## Skyweaver and Multi-Domain Mission Autonomy
- **Edge GPU Processing at Altitude:** **Matt McCue** introduced *Skyweaver*, an agentic AI orchestration platform running on hardware stacks including GPUs operating at **up to 70,000 feet** on stratospheric balloons and **30,000 feet** on *Ultra* aircraft.
- **Gulf of America Domain Awareness Use Case:** **Ryan Hartman** presented a concrete operational scenario where stratospheric balloons provide wide-area imaging over **750 square miles of open ocean**, using edge AI to classify vessel types, autonomously task *Ultra* UAVs for high-resolution confirmation, and package intelligence products for human analysts in **single-digit minutes** instead of hours.
- **Human-on-the-Loop Governance:** **Ryan Hartman** emphasized that human operators maintain continuous oversight ("human on the loop" rather than in the loop), retaining complete chain of custody and the ability to override autonomous tasking at any point during detection, tracking, and prosecution workflows.

## Notable Quotes
> "Advantage now belongs to whomever can deploy autonomous systems at scale."
> — **Eric (Ondas CEO, quoted by Tom McArdle)**

> "When you hear about Patriot missiles being used on $35,000 needs, the taxpayer, which we all are, is absolutely crying inside every time that happens."
> — **Matt McCue**

> "We're going to demonstrate on what it looks like for 1 + 1 to equal 10 or 11 or 12... because we're moving fast, and we're doing it with a level of effectiveness that I think is going to be amazing."
> — **Ryan Hartman**

> "At the end of the day, the chemistry and the battery drives the endurance of the airplane... don't lose sight on the hardware."
> — **Matt McCue**

briefings.title: Shaping the Future of AI Through Openness: A Fireside Chat with Lisa Su and Clem Delangue
briefings.tldr: AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su and Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue discussed how open models, accessible local compute, and developer collaboration are accelerating the agentic AI era.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su and Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue discussed how open models, accessible local compute, and developer collaboration are accelerating the agentic AI era. They highlighted new hardware-software integrations like the Ryzen AI Max platform and emphasized transforming people from passive AI users into active AI builders.

## Hugging Face Platform Growth & Diversification
* **Massive Public Repository Scale:** 
  * **3 Million Public Models:** Hosted on the Hugging Face platform alongside 1 million public datasets and nearly as many private ones (Clem Delangue).
  * **Rapid Upload Velocity:** One new repository is created on Hugging Face every seven seconds (Clem Delangue).
* **Domain Expansion Beyond Text:** 
  * **Multimodal Growth:** Significant activity is now occurring in video, images, biology, chemistry, and robotics, signaling AI's transformation across all global domains (Clem Delangue).

## The Importance of Openness in Agentic AI
* **Transparency and Control:** 
  * **Autonomy Requires Oversight:** Autonomy without transparency, control, and understanding is risky, dangerous, and problematic (Clem Delangue).
  * **Avoiding Black Boxes:** Companies cannot outsource their agents to a black box; they need open models to own, inspect, and understand how their agents work and perform (Clem Delangue).
* **Ecosystem Diversity:** 
  * **No Single Monopoly on Ideas:** No single company, group, chip, or model holds all the good ideas, requiring an open ecosystem to mix and match computing for diverse workloads and industries (Lisa Su).
  * **Flexibility:** Open ecosystems ensure developers are not tied down to a single underlying architecture when better technology emerges (Lisa Su).

## Local Compute, Accessibility, and Hardware Partnerships
* **Shift Toward Local AI Workloads:** 
  * **Resurgence of Local Dev Stations:** Driven by a desire to build on local hardware, developers want to understand which models fit specific hardware, quantify them, and optimize them for better tokens-per-dollar (Clem Delangue).
  * **AMD-Hugging Face Hardware Integration:** Jack announced a new platform combining Ryzen AI Max and Hugging Face to make leading-edge AI hardware barrier-free (Lisa Su, referencing Jack).
* **Practical Edge Computing:** 
  * **Offline Accessibility:** Local hardware like AI PCs and the Ryzen AI Max "Halo box" solve real-world productivity issues, such as maintaining AI access while traveling on planes with failing Wi-Fi (Lisa Su).

## Robotics, Edge Experiments, and Democratization
* **Physical World Interaction:** 
  * **Richie Mini Robot:** Hugging Face shipped over 10,000 units of the "Richie Mini" robot worldwide as an experiment, allowing visual interaction and real-world dataset collection to improve system reasoning (Clem Delangue).
* **Empowering Software Engineers:** 
  * **Lowering Barriers:** Software engineers can now act as AI builders rather than just AI users—optimizing, running, experimenting, and training models (Clem Delangue).
  * **Small Teams, Big Ideas:** Five people with a good idea can leverage open models and accessible hardware to build amazing solutions without needing thousands of employees or tens of thousands of GPUs (Lisa Su).

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Model Count Explosion:** Clem Delangue predicts that in the next few years, the ecosystem will move from 3 million models toward **hundreds of millions of different models**—approaching a scale where there are as many models as specific use cases, companies, or even individual people.

## Notable Quotes
* > "You can't really outsource your agents to a black box. So all of that I think shows the importance of openness for agents."
  > — Clem Delangue

* > "I'm a firm believer in there's no one company that has all of the good ideas. There's no one group. There's no one chip. There's no one model that's the best."
  > — Lisa Su

* > "The difference is you can either choose to be a part of it, or you can choose to be afraid of it. And choosing to be a part of it means that you're actually empowered with the most capable technology that you can imagine."
  > — Lisa Su

briefings.title: Susan Cain: Why Introverts Make Great Leaders | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: Susan Cain, author of Quiet and Bittersweet, joins Nicolai Tangen, CEO of Norges Bank Investment Management, to discuss personality, leadership, the impact of AI, and why introverts and highly sensitive people bring unique strengths to the modern world.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Susan Cain, author of *Quiet* and *Bittersweet*, joins Nicolai Tangen, CEO of Norges Bank Investment Management, to discuss personality, leadership, the impact of AI, and why introverts and highly sensitive people bring unique strengths to the modern world.

## The Future of Introverts and Highly Sensitive People in the Age of AI
* **The AI Outlook:** **Wait-and-See Approach:** Cain adopts a cautious view on AI, noting that while technology initially offers multi-channel communication for introverts, it often devolves into platforms for cultural self-presentation.
* **High Agency:** **Goal-Directed Focus:** Introverts possess high agency directed toward specific, deeply held goals rather than broadcasting widely, allowing them to effectively leverage AI for focused projects.
* **Highly Sensitive People (HSPs):** **The 15–20% Advantage:** Representing 15% to 20% of the population, HSPs have nervous systems that react more intensely to all forms of stimulation (both positive and negative) and possess a deep appreciation for excellence and authenticity.
    * **Robot-Proof Authenticity:** Because HSPs naturally reject inauthenticity, Cain predicts they will hold a major advantage in an AI-driven decade where human-to-human connection and genuine self-expression become premium commodities.

## Personality, Culture, and the Evolution of Social Media
* **Culture of Character vs. Personality:** **The 20th-Century Shift:** Around the turn of the 20th century, Western society shifted from a "culture of character" (valuing inner worth, integrity, and small communities) to a "culture of personality" (valuing magnetism, charisma, and public presentation).
* **Social Media Amplification:** Platforms that began as networking tools for old friends have evolved into amplified platforms for self-presentation, fostering an overloaded culture of curated packaging.
* **Geographic Differences:** **Cultural Values:** The United States leans toward valuing extroversion, whereas Confucian societies place higher value on introversion and group harmony (encapsulated by the aphorism: *"The wind howls and the mountain remains still"*).

## Temperament, Leadership, and Office Dynamics
* **Biological Roots:** **Nature and Nurture:** Introversion, extroversion, and high sensitivity are among the most heritable traits; studies show newborn infants who salivate more to sugar water (indicating higher nervous system reactivity) grow up to be quieter children who observe environments before engaging.
* **Leadership Outcomes:** **Quiet Success:** Research by Jim Collins (*Good to Great*) showed that 11 of the top-performing CEOs in the U.S. were described as quiet, shy, and unassuming, yet fiercely dedicated to their companies.
    * **Douglas Conant Example:** As CEO of Campbell Soup, shy introvert Douglas Conant wrote **30,000 personal gratitude letters** to employees over **10 years**.
    * **Adam Grant’s Research:** Extroverted leaders drive better outcomes when employees lack motivation, whereas introverted leaders deliver superior results when working with proactive employees because they actively listen to and integrate their ideas.
* **Meeting Dynamics:** **Dominant Voices:** A Kellogg School of Business study found that in typical large meetings, **three people do 70% of the talking**, often drowning out diverse ideas.
* **Workplace Design:** To prevent burnout, companies must balance stimulation by providing both collaborative spaces and quiet, uninterrupted focus zones.

## Bittersweetness, Toxic Positivity, and Organizational Culture
* **The Bittersweet Outlook:** **Joy and Sorrow:** Cain defines a bittersweet personality as one that recognizes the co-existence of joy and sorrow, which fosters a richer appreciation of life and human fragility.
* **Toxic Positivity:** **The Cost of Forced Happiness:** The unspoken corporate demand for relentless happiness drains cognitive energy and prevents genuine connection.
* **Gulf of Mexico Oil Rig Study:** Harvard Business School research on an oil rig showed that when CEO Rick Fox replaced a culture of forced toughness with open communication about personal challenges and operational doubts, **accident rates plummeted** and **productivity increased significantly**.

## Notable Quotes
> *"The most robotproof people are going to be the ones who care very deeply about maintaining human authenticity... that's going to be the big commodity in the next decade."*
> — **Susan Cain**

> *"In your typical large meeting you have three people doing 70% of the talking. And that is a disaster if you assume that on average everyone has the same number of good and bad ideas."*
> — **Susan Cain**

> *"My advice to young people is to think about what did you really love and who were you really when you were a child? Because that gives you the clue to who you really are."*
> — **Susan Cain**

briefings.title: The Case for Data Centers in Space
briefings.tldr: Starcloud is building space-based data centers to bypass terrestrial energy and regulatory constraints, achieving a billion-dollar valuation just 17 months after YC demo day.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Starcloud is building space-based data centers to bypass terrestrial energy and regulatory constraints, achieving a billion-dollar valuation just 17 months after YC demo day. Founded by Philip Johnston, the company successfully trained the first large language model in space in November 2025 and has filed with the FCC to deploy 88,000 satellites.

## Origin Story & Strategic Pivot
- **Founding Background:** Philip Johnston founded Starcloud on January 1, 2024, after recognizing plummeting launch costs during a 2023 visit to Starbase Texas where SpaceX was building gigafactories to produce up to three Starships per day.
- **Initial Concept:** The company initially launched as *Lumin orbit* in January 2024 to pursue space-based solar power, inspired by Isaac Asimov and 1960s sci-fi concepts.
- **The Pivot to Data Centers:** After discovering that space-based solar power loses 95% of energy during transmission from space to Earth, Johnston and the team recalculated break-even costs. While space-based solar required a drop to $50 per kilo, data centers made economic sense at a break-even launch cost of $500 per kilo, prompting an immediate pivot.
- **Rejected Concepts:** The team evaluated and rejected asteroid mining, space manufacturing, and space hotels because they require expensive and complex re-entry processes, whereas data centers do not.

## Starcloud-1 Mission & Engineering Breakthroughs
- **The Launch Strategy:** On January 2, 2024 (the day after founding), Starcloud booked the first available SpaceX rideshare launch as a forcing function, 18 to 21 months out, before knowing exactly what payload they would fly.
- **Starcloud-1 Metrics:** Launched in November 2025, the mission cost $2 million total (compared to prime contractor quotes of $75M to $100M). The team of 12 traveled to Florida to watch it lift off at midnight.
- **Hardware on Orbit:** Starcloud-1 carried five GPUs (three from Nvidia, two from ARM), including an Nvidia H100. 
- **Thermal Management Innovation:** To solve the extreme power density and heat of the H100 in a vacuum, Starcloud submerged all components, power delivery systems, and memory in a phase change material for immersion cooling. 
- **Pre-Launch Crunch:** Facing a tight deadline without time to reserve a proper vacuum thermal chamber, co-founder Ezra built a makeshift thermal cycle test using ice baths and hair dryers/hot air guns at 5:00 AM on launch day.
- **On-Orbit Commissioning:** Following deployment (featured on a 5-story screen by Jensen Huang at GTC 2025), the satellite required 12 hours for first contact and a grueling 3-day troubleshooting cycle to resolve a repeating restart loop triggered by one of 20 failure modes.
- **First Space Milestones:** Starcloud successfully trained the first large language model in space, ran the first version of Gemini, fine-tuned a model on orbit, and performed high-power inference on satellite imagery.

## Roadmap & Constellation Plans
- **Starcloud-2 (Next 20 Satellites):** A 10-kilowatt spacecraft equipped with three SpaceX Starlink laser terminals for high bandwidth and low latency. It will fly a Bitcoin mining ASIC, more H100s, Blackwell chips, and AWS Outposts hardware (on-premises server blades for local VC2 instances, tailored for military customers).
- **Starcloud-3 and Beyond:** A 200-kilowatt, 3-ton spacecraft measuring about 6 meters long. Fifty of these can fit inside a single Starship, generating approximately 10 megawatts of new compute capacity per flight.
- **FCC Filing:** Starcloud has filed with the FCC for a constellation of 88,000 satellites, projected to provide roughly 20 gigawatts of new compute capacity.

## Engineering Challenges & Hardware Trade-Offs
- **Thermal Dissipation:** Split 50/50 with radiation, the primary engineering hurdle is heat rejection in a vacuum. Starcloud designed a deployable liquid-cooled radiator that is 10 times less mass per watt and 500 times less cost per watt than the International Space Station's radiator.
- **Radiation Hardening:** Rather than using expensive space-graded components, Starcloud uses off-the-shelf automotive-style parts. They conduct rigorous heavy-ion testing at Brookhaven National Laboratory and high-velocity proton testing at the Knoxville cyclotron to expose hardware to 5-year mission doses in 24 hours.
- **DC-to-DC Architecture:** Solar panels generate direct current (DC) immediately, eliminating energy losses from traditional AC-to-DC conversions. 

## Fundraising & Market Dynamics
- **Initial Rejection:** The seed round in late 2023 sought $2 million at a $10 million post-money valuation on a SAFE. It took three months, and roughly 100 VCs rejected the idea as too sci-fi. After YC Demo Day, they faced at least 20 more rejections before securing their first check.
- **Benchmark Partnership:** Starcloud became Benchmark's first-ever space investment. Chathan led the round after conducting deep technical due diligence on the engineering team. The round faced complications mid-process when SpaceX privately indicated they were exploring similar concepts, triggering conflict-of-interest policies for multiple VCs.
- **The Hard Tech Shift:** Johnston notes a rapid public market sentiment shift against traditional SaaS moats (accelerated by tools like Claude code), which quickly translated into investor appetite for deep tech and hard tech.
- **Hiring Rigor:** Despite raising significant capital (including a large round following their March announcement), the company maintains a tight-knit engineering team of only 20 engineers and one commercial lead from the Space Force (formerly working on Golden Dome), deliberately moving slowly and selectively on hires.

## Notable Quotes
> "The first thing every space company should do is book the first available launch they can... before they built the thing. Before they probably even know what they're going to launch. Booking a launch is such a good forcing function for a space company."
> — **Philip Johnston**

> "It is a miracle that it works to be honest. You can just do things... That's the kind of thing you can do as a startup because we actually had a quote from one of the primes on what it would cost to do StarCloud 1 and they said $75 million to $100 million and we did the whole of Starcloud 2 [Starcloud-1] including the launch for $2 million."
> — **Philip Johnston**

> "For a very long time, their reactions was, 'this is the dumbest thing I've ever heard.' ... This is one of these ideas that was like extremely unpopular with investors and if you had listened to what all the investors were telling you, you would have quit and not ever done this idea."
> — **Philip Johnston**

briefings.title: The Nuclear Renaissance - Radiant |  a16z American Dynamism
briefings.tldr: Radiant is developing portable, factory-built nuclear microreactors called Kaleidos to provide clean, reliable, and accessible power for remote communities, data centers, national security needs, and space exploration.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Radiant is developing portable, factory-built nuclear microreactors called Kaleidos to provide clean, reliable, and accessible power for remote communities, data centers, national security needs, and space exploration. By shifting from on-site construction to mass production in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, the company aims to eliminate the high costs and logistical complexities that have historically stalled the nuclear industry.

## The State of Energy and the Nuclear Industry
* **Aging and Strained Grid:** 
  * The current U.S. power grid was largely built in the 1960s and 1970s and is increasingly showing its age.
  * **High Outage Rate:** Approximately 45% of Americans have experienced at least one power outage in the past year, which can be catastrophic for businesses.
  * **Energy Deficit Risk:** Society currently runs near the median of required power, leaving many states dipping below energy needs during peak times and stifling innovation.
* **Historical Decline of Nuclear:**
  * **Lost Momentum:** The U.S. built 52 nuclear reactors at Idaho National Laboratory over a 21-year span, but the last one was completed in 1977, and none have been built there since.
  * **Regulatory Overburden:** Nuclear energy was heavily sidelined by environmental misinformation and a mounting stack of regulations, effectively pricing the technology out of business.
  * **On-Site Construction Flaws:** Traditional nuclear projects require massive holes dug in the ground, causing unpredictable costs, timeline overruns, and permanent radiological designation for the site.

## The Kaleidos Microreactor Product & Factory Model
* **The Kaleidos Design:**
  * **Size and Portability:** A transportable microreactor that fits on the back of an 18-wheeler and can be moved by land, air, and sea.
  * **Diesel Generator Analogy:** Comparable in size to a diesel generator, but delivers many times more power and operates for 5 years without needing refueling.
  * **Daisy-Chaining Capability:** Four Kaleidos units can be linked together to power a small city or a very large data center.
* **Frictionless Customer Experience:**
  * **Apple-Like Simplicity:** Built to eliminate customer friction by handling all burdens—including construction, interconnects, and waste management.
  * **Return-to-Factory Refueling:** After a 5-year operational window, the unit is shipped back to Radiant’s factory in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, for refueling, ensuring customers never have to deal with waste on site.
* **Factory-Built Advantage:**
  * **Cost Control:** Moving from construction projects to factory mass production removes on-site uncertainties and shifts financial risk into the manufacturing process, turning reactors into predictable commodities.
  * **Target Scale:** The long-term vision is to produce one nuclear reactor per week off a standard production line.

## Origins, National Security, and Expanding Use Cases
* **Space Exploration Roots:**
  * **SpaceX Heritage:** Founder Doug Bernauer worked at SpaceX for about 12 years on the Mars challenge to make life multilanetary.
  * **The Energy Bottleneck:** Realizing that solar power on Mars was insufficient to make fuel and return via Starship, Bernauer determined that nuclear power was the only viable solution, leading him to found Radiant.
* **National Security & Energy Independence:**
  * **Avoiding Foreign Dependencies:** Countries relying on adversaries for energy have strings attached that can cause entire nations to shut down during conflicts.
  * **Rapid Deployment:** Microreactors can be deployed rapidly alongside AI infrastructure, drones, or military operations where grid power is unavailable.
* **Novel Use Cases:** 
  * Providing power in boxes that fit in a few parking spaces unlocks entirely new applications, such as high-altitude camps on Mount Everest or cities on the bottom of the ocean.

## Upcoming Milestones and Prototype Testing
* **Idaho National Laboratory Partnership:**
  * **Historic Location:** Radiant is taking its unit to a dome structure built in the 1950s at Idaho National Laboratory that originally housed the Experimental Breeder Reactor and was slated for teardown.
  * **Competitive Selection:** Radiant was selected through a competitive process as the first company to test in this repurposed facility.
  * **Testing Plan:** Since 2020, the company has targeted 2026 to bring the system to the dome, go critical, reach temperatures over 700°C, and run continuously for 150 hours at full power.
* **Regulatory Support:** Executive orders signed by the President in May of the prior year accelerated the entire process, supporting Radiant in the race to turn on the world's first commercial microreactor.

## Notable Quotes
> "When Doug was designing the product, he said, 'All of these things must be true, and therefore I have to make a product that is above ground, that is movable to where customers need it, and then also that they don't have to deal with waste on site.' And so, you got Kaleidos."
> — **Tori Shivanandan**

> "One of our units is 5 years of power in a box that just gets delivered, fits in a few parking spaces, and then whenever you want us to take it away, we take it away, which hasn't really been done before."
> — **Doug Bernauer**

> "The world is watching, but the world is waiting. And there are many companies that want to deploy, but they just don't want to be first. And Radiant is willing to be first and has the courage to take those calculated risks."
> — **Tori Shivanandan**
